capabilities: Open the terminal at the vault root or the active note's folder
Launch coding-agent CLIs with an optional prompt containing the current note path
Run Git commit-and-push and pull commands from the vault root
Configure per-platform terminal applications, including WSL on Windows
extras: Desktop only and requires Obsidian 1.5.0 or later. Agent and Git commands are off by default and must be enabled in settings. Uses child_process and direct fs access (temp launch scripts) as disclosed under Obsidian developer policies; makes no network requests of its own.
motivation: The author notes that a vault is a folder of Markdown files, which is what coding agents and Git work best with, and that getting there normally means opening a terminal, finding the vault path and typing cd.
problem: Obsidian offers no built-in way to open a terminal at the vault path or hand the current note to a coding-agent CLI, so users must find the folder and type cd manually.
